name: The Hundred
shortDescription: A breath-driven warm-up that engages the abdominals while pumping the arms and stabilizing the ribcage.
benefits: Improves lung capacity and steady core support through intentional breath pacing.
modifications: Keep the head on the mat and legs lower to reduce cervical strain and core load.
Perform single-leg pumps or supported heel taps if full leg extension is too intense.
progressions: Extend the legs higher while keeping the pelvis stable.
Increase arm speed slightly once breath coordination is steady.

name: Roll Up
shortDescription: Sequential spinal articulation from supine to seated that builds core strength while lengthening the back.
benefits: Builds deep abdominal control while teaching safe spinal articulation.
modifications: Bend the knees and use the arms to support the spine during the roll-up.
Start with a tabletop prep variation if hamstring flexibility is limited.
progressions: Perform with straight legs and less use of the arms.
Lift the arms overhead to increase the challenge once the spine is stable.

name: Roll Over
shortDescription: Controlled inversion and spine mobility exercise that opens the back line and stretches the hamstrings.
benefits: Enhances back flexibility and helps stretch the posterior chain.
modifications: Keep the legs bent and move with a smaller range of motion to protect the hamstrings and lower back.
Use the arms to support the motion and roll only as far as the shoulders allow.
progressions: Straighten the legs more gradually as hamstring flexibility improves.
Lower the legs more slowly toward vertical while keeping the spine controlled.

name: Rolling Like a Ball
shortDescription: Rounded rolling movement that massages the spine, challenges balance, and coordinates breath with motion.
benefits: Develops balance, spine mobility, and circular movement control.
modifications: Keep the feet on the mat or hold the shins instead of the ankles to reduce strain.
Use a smaller rocking range and focus on maintaining a rounded spine.
progressions: Increase balance challenge by rocking with a slightly smaller base of support.
Add a small pause at the top of the rock before rolling back.

name: Spine Stretch Forward
shortDescription: Seated forward stretch with dynamic spinal flexion and hamstring length, emphasizing posture and ribcage control.
benefits: Promotes spinal flexion with hamstring length and posture awareness.
modifications: Sit on a small block or cushion to ease hamstring stretch.
Bend the knees slightly and reach only as far as the spine can stay long.
progressions: Extend the legs further and reach the arms farther past the feet.
Hold the longer position with a steady breath and a strong core.

name: Roll Down
shortDescription: Sequential spinal articulation from standing to mat that mobilizes the spine and lengthens the back.
benefits: Improves segmental spine mobility while reinforcing deep abdominal support.
modifications: Bend the knees slightly and move slower if hamstring flexibility is limited.
Keep the arms long and the shoulders relaxed away from the ears.
progressions: Work toward a slower, fully articulated roll-down with longer inhalations between each segment.
Add a small arm reach forward at the bottom to increase spinal length and control.

name: Teaser
shortDescription: Classic V-shape lift demanding core precision, hip flexor coordination, and a long, supported spine.
benefits: Strengthens the full core and challenges coordination in a balanced lift.
modifications: Practice with bent knees and support the thighs with the hands.
Lift only as high as the lower back can stay long and stable.
progressions: Straighten the legs and lower the arms overhead with control.
Hold the top position for a longer count while maintaining breath.

name: Saw
shortDescription: Seated rotation with spinal flexion that stretches the hamstrings and obliques while maintaining a stable pelvis.
benefits: Improves rotational mobility and encourages a long, stable spine.
modifications: Reduce the twist range and keep the spine long rather than collapsing.
Shorten the leg separation if the hamstrings feel too tight.
progressions: Reach farther past the feet and deepen the rotation with a stable torso.
Increase the reach while keeping the ribs lifted over the hips.

name: Corkscrew
shortDescription: Supine hip circle exercise for lower abdominal control and gentle spinal articulation through rotation.
benefits: Targets lower abdominal support and gentle hip mobility.
modifications: Keep the legs higher and use smaller circles to protect the lower back.
Keep the shoulders grounded and move slowly with control.
progressions: Lengthen the descent of the legs and increase the circle size gradually.
Slow the motion and focus on steady torso stabilization through each rotation.

name: Jackknife
shortDescription: Advanced bridge-to-inversion that articulates the spine and hips while challenging control and shoulder stability.
benefits: Builds control through inverted spine articulation and hip lift.
modifications: Use bridge prep and lift the hips only as high as comfortable.
Keep the knees slightly bent and avoid straining the lower back.
progressions: Work toward a higher hip lift and a fuller roll onto the shoulders.
Slowly lower back down with control rather than dropping through the spine.

name: Neck Pull
shortDescription: Torso lift from supine using abdominal strength to articulate the spine while maintaining neck length.
benefits: Supports core-driven upper spinal articulation without neck strain.
modifications: Keep the hands behind the head and avoid pulling on the neck.
Maintain a small chin tuck and only lift as far as the abdominals can support.
progressions: Lower the legs closer to the mat while keeping the spine articulated.
Extend the arms overhead as core control improves.

name: Spine Twist
shortDescription: Seated rotational mobility movement that maintains pelvic stability while opening the torso and shoulders.
benefits: Increases seated spine rotation while maintaining pelvic stability.
modifications: Bend the knees and shorten the leg separation to reduce torque.
Keep the hips stable and rotate only as far as the spine stays tall.
progressions: Extend the legs farther and deepen the twist while keeping the ribs lifted.
Look over the leading shoulder to lengthen through the spine and neck.

name: Side Bend
shortDescription: Lateral flexion exercise that stretches the side body and strengthens the obliques with a long torso line.
benefits: Lengthens the side body and strengthens lateral core support.
modifications: Keep the bottom elbow slightly bent and use a smaller side-bend arc.
Avoid collapsing into the lower ribs by keeping the side body long.
progressions: Lift higher through the top arm and deepen the side stretch safely.
Extend the legs more fully while maintaining a strong base on the mat.

name: Boomerang
shortDescription: Dynamic rolling balance combining twist, hip lift and coordination in a flowing V-sit shape.
benefits: Boosts coordination, balance, and dynamic postural control.
modifications: Practice teaser and roll-up prep first, and keep the rotation smaller.
Move slowly through the transition and keep the legs closer together.
progressions: Increase the leg switch speed while maintaining control.
Deepen the roll-through portion with a longer balanced hold.

name: Swan
shortDescription: Prone back extension that lifts the chest while maintaining a long neck and stable pelvis.
benefits: Builds spinal extension, shoulder strength, and posterior chain coordination.
modifications: Keep the forearms on the mat and lift only as far as comfortable.
Support the chest with the hands if the lower back feels sensitive.
progressions: Extend the arms further and lift higher while keeping the neck long.
Slow the lift-lower rhythm to reinforce control through the back.

name: Swan Prep
shortDescription: Gentle prone extension prep that warms the back and strengthens the upper spine with less range.
focus: Spinal extension preparation and shoulder stability.
benefits: Prepares the back for full swan by activating the posterior muscles safely.
modifications: Keep the forearms on the mat and lift only a few inches.
Use a smaller range of motion and keep the ribs broad.
progressions: Move toward full arm extension while keeping the ribs lifted.
Increase lift height gradually as back strength improves.

name: Swan Dive
shortDescription: Prone extension that lifts the chest and legs with fluid spine movement and length through the back.
focus: Back extension and posterior chain strengthening.
benefits: Strengthens the back line and encourages fluid extension.
modifications: Keep the chest lower and lift only as high as the back can support.
Keep the knees soft and avoid overarching the lower spine.
progressions: Lift higher and extend the spine more fully in the glide.
Lengthen the arms forward and maintain a strong shoulder line.

name: Swimming
shortDescription: Prone alternate arm and leg lifts that tone the posterior chain and encourage coordinated breath.
benefits: Tones the posterior chain and improves breath-synchronized movement.
modifications: Alternate arm and leg lifts rather than lifting all limbs at once.
Keep the head down if neck mobility is sensitive.
progressions: Lift both arms and legs higher while maintaining a long spine.
Increase the speed slightly while keeping the movement smooth and rhythmic.

name: Shoulder Bridge
shortDescription: Pelvic articulation exercise that mobilizes the spine and engages the hamstrings from a supported shoulder base.
benefits: Mobilizes the spine and activates glutes with controlled lifting.
modifications: Keep the hips lower and use hands for support if needed.
Widen the feet and soften the lift to reduce strain on the spine.
progressions: Lift higher into the bridge with stronger hamstring engagement.
Add single-leg bridge work once the basic bridge feels stable.

name: Leg Pull Front
shortDescription: Plank-based leg lift that strengthens the core, glutes and shoulders while promoting full-body alignment.
benefits: Challenges full-body alignment and shoulder-core integration.
modifications: Drop the knees to the mat and shorten the plank position.
Keep the hips level and avoid letting the lower back sag.
progressions: Work toward a full straight-leg plank with a longer hold.
Lift one leg higher while maintaining shoulder stability and neutral spine.

name: Leg Pull Back
shortDescription: Prone leg lift movement that trains lower back support, glute control and stable shoulder placement.
benefits: Reinforces lower back support and glute engagement in prone extension.
modifications: Keep the knees bent or start on the elbows to reduce load.
Use smaller leg lifts and keep the core engaged to avoid arching.
progressions: Progress to full straight legs with a stable pelvis.
Hold the lifted position longer while maintaining even breathing.

name: Side Kick
shortDescription: Side-lying leg movement that strengthens the hip and stabilizes the supporting body line.
benefits: Improves hip strength and balance while training precise leg extension.
modifications: Keep the top leg lower and use smaller movements until control improves.
Support the head with the upper hand to maintain neck comfort.
progressions: Straighten the top leg and lift it higher with precision.
Add small pulses or a longer hold at the top for extra control.

name: Side Kick Series
shortDescription: Side-lying leg sequence focusing on hip stability, precise control, and long supporting posture.
benefits: Sharpens hip stability and precise leg control in side-lying work.
modifications: Keep the kicks smaller and support the head with the upper hand.
Slow the tempo to focus on controlled hip alignment.
progressions: Increase leg height and lengthen the range of motion.
Add a slight pulse at the top of each kick with a stable torso.

name: Seal
shortDescription: Playful rounded rolling exercise that combines balance, breath, and spinal rounding with rhythmic clapping.
benefits: Builds coordination and spine articulation through playful rolling.
modifications: Keep the feet closer together and use smaller rocks.
Limit the clap depth and avoid bouncing too aggressively.
progressions: Rock with a slightly larger base of support and longer hold between rocks.
Increase the circle size while keeping the spine rounded and shoulders relaxed.

name: Crab
shortDescription: Supine roll with legs overhead that challenges spinal articulation, shoulder support, and breath rhythm.
benefits: Enhances spinal mobility with shoulder stability in a rolling balance.
modifications: Make the leg circles smaller and keep the shoulders grounded.
Move slowly and avoid lifting the hip too high.
progressions: Perform larger leg circles with more control through the hip joint.
Extend the leg longer while maintaining a stable upper body.

name: Rocking
shortDescription: Back roll from supine to seated and back that tunes spinal articulation, balance, and rhythm.
benefits: Improves control through spinal rolling and balance in dynamic transitions.
modifications: Keep the legs closer together and use smaller rolls.
Focus on staying rounded and moving with steady breath.
progressions: Increase the roll height and pause at the top with control.
Make the transition smoother by lengthening the inhale and exhale.

name: Control Balance
shortDescription: Advanced inversion that tests balance, hip control, and maintaining a long spine in a lifted position.
benefits: Tests balance and lower back strength in a lifted inversion.
modifications: Keep one leg lower and use the hands lightly for balance if needed.
Avoid forcing the inverted position and focus on core stability.
progressions: Straighten both legs more fully with a controlled lift.
Hold the position longer while maintaining length through the spine.

name: Scissors
shortDescription: Supine alternating leg stretch that opens the hamstrings while preserving a stable trunk and pelvis.
benefits: Strengthens abdominal support while deepening hamstring stretch.
modifications: Keep the head down and bend the lower knee slightly.
Use a smaller leg separation to reduce hamstring strain.
progressions: Straighten both legs more and lower the bottom leg closer to the mat.
Increase the rhythmic coordination with a stronger abdominal draw-in.

name: Bicycle
shortDescription: Alternating supine leg cycling that strengthens the core and promotes controlled spinal stability.
benefits: Develops core endurance and controlled lower-body rotation.
modifications: Keep the lower leg higher and move more slowly for better control.
Soften the neck and avoid lifting the head excessively.
progressions: Increase the range of motion and keep the breath steady.
Circle the arms and legs with more coordination and a longer spine.

name: One Leg Circle
shortDescription: Single-leg hip circle from supine that develops pelvic stability and hip joint mobility.
benefits: Improves hip mobility while maintaining a stable torso and pelvis.
modifications: Bend the supporting knee slightly and use smaller circles.
Focus on stabilizing the hips rather than the size of the leg circle.
progressions: Perform larger circles with a longer supporting leg.
Keep the standing hip stable while the moving leg circles.

name: Single Leg Stretch
shortDescription: Alternating knee draw-ins that coordinate breath with abdominal engagement and hip stability.
focus: Core coordination and hip flexor control.
benefits: Builds coordination between breath, core, and leg movement.
modifications: Keep the head down and work one leg at a time with smaller range.
Shorten the leg extension to maintain lower back stability.
progressions: Extend the legs farther and increase coordination with breath.
Move more smoothly between legs with a stronger core hold.

name: Double Leg Stretch
shortDescription: Full-body extension requiring precise timing, core support, and smooth breath coordination.
benefits: Encourages full-body length and coordinated abdominal support.
modifications: Keep the head down and use a smaller arm and leg circle.
Limit the range of motion if the lower back feels unstable.
progressions: Extend the arms overhead and lower the legs deeper with control.
Widen the circle as strength improves while maintaining coordination.

name: Open Leg Rocker
shortDescription: Rolling balance exercise with open legs that challenges core control, spine articulation, and lengthening.
benefits: Tests balance, core strength, and spine articulation in rolling.
modifications: Use a smaller rocking range and practice teaser prep first.
Keep the legs closer together and maintain a stable spine.
progressions: Increase the rocking height and balance with a longer hold at the top.
Lengthen the legs and deepen the spine articulation through the motion.

name: Hip Circles
shortDescription: Controlled hip rotation movement that mobilizes the pelvis while engaging the core for stability.
benefits: Mobilizes the hips while reinforcing core stability.
modifications: Use smaller leg swings and keep the hips stable.
Support the head with the upper hand if needed.
progressions: Increase circle size while keeping the torso still.
Keep the spine long and avoid leaning into the supporting side.

name: Hip Twist
shortDescription: Seated rotation with lifted legs that trains oblique strength and pelvic control.
benefits: Develops torso rotation while stabilizing the pelvis and lower abdominals.
modifications: Keep the legs lower and the twist smaller if the lower back feels sensitive.
Sit on a cushion to help maintain a tall spine.
progressions: Lift the legs higher and deepen the twist with stable hips.
Hold the legs in the air longer while maintaining torso control.

name: One Leg Kick
shortDescription: Prone leg kick series that strengthens the hamstrings and chest while keeping the spine long and shoulders grounded.
focus: Posterior chain strength and shoulder stability.
benefits: Strengthens hamstrings and shoulders in a controlled prone position.
modifications: Keep the knees wider and use smaller kick pulses.
Support the head lightly with the top hand to reduce neck strain.
progressions: Straighten the moving leg more and increase the kick range.
Speed up the rhythm slightly while maintaining control.

name: Double Leg Kick
shortDescription: Prone chest lift with leg kicks, blending spinal extension with shoulder stability and rhythmic breath.
benefits: Combines back extension with upper-body stability and rhythm.
modifications: Keep the head down and use smaller lifts and kicks.
Soften the arch and focus on engaging the upper back.
progressions: Lift higher and kick stronger with a longer spinal extension.
Lengthen the arms and keep the shoulder blades wide.

name: Knee Stretch
shortDescription: Kneeling knee circles that enhance pelvic stability, leg control, and mindful abdominal engagement.
benefits: Fortifies pelvic stability and smooth leg coordination in kneeling.
modifications: Tuck the knees more and keep the hands on the bar for support.
Reduce the depth of the round-back motion to stay comfortable.
progressions: Increase the round-back range and deepen the motion.
Add a longer hold at the end of the stretch to build stability.

name: Side Kick Kneeling
shortDescription: Kneeling side-leg lift that challenges hip stability and control through the standing leg.
benefits: Builds hip strength and core stability while training balance in kneeling.
modifications: Keep the movements smaller and the supporting hand grounded for extra stability.
Lower the lifted leg slightly if balance feels unstable.
progressions: Increase leg height while maintaining a stable kneeling base.
Add a small pulse at the top to deepen hip control.

name: Pelvic Curl
shortDescription: Articulated bridge movement that mobilizes the spine, activates the glutes, and lengthens the back body.
benefits: Articulates the spine while activating glutes and posterior chain.
modifications: Lift only partway and keep the motion small and controlled.
Use the arms and feet for support if the lower back feels tight.
progressions: Roll through the spine more fully and lift higher into bridge.
Hold the top position longer with a stronger hamstring engagement.

name: Shoulder Rolls
shortDescription: Gentle circular shoulder mobility that releases tension and prepares the upper body for movement.
benefits: Improves shoulder range of motion and reduces stiffness before Pilates practice.
modifications: Keep the circles small and slow if the neck or shoulders feel tight.
Perform the movement seated or standing with the spine long and relaxed.
progressions: Increase the circle size gradually while maintaining a relaxed neck.
Add a gentle arm swing between rolls to mobilize the shoulder blades.

name: Spine Mobilization
shortDescription: Slow spinal flexion and extension from a seated position to warm up the spine and awaken the core.
benefits: Prepares the back and torso for exercise by improving segmental movement and breath coordination.
modifications: Move through a smaller range of motion and keep the breath easy.
Use a cushion under the hips if sitting tall is uncomfortable.
progressions: Increase the depth of the flexion and extension while maintaining control.
Add a slight twist at the top of the movement for added thoracic mobility.

name: Seated Side Bend
shortDescription: Long side-body stretch performed from a seated position to release tension and lengthen the waist.
benefits: Opens the ribcage and side body while supporting gentle release after movement.
modifications: Keep the bottom hand light on the floor and reach the top arm gently.
Bend the knees slightly if the hips feel tight in the seated position.
progressions: Reach the top arm farther and lengthen through both sides of the waist.
Add a small twist toward the front leg while keeping the spine long.

name: Breaststroke
shortDescription: Prone arm and leg extension performed with gentle torso lift and steady breath rhythm.
focus: Posterior chain extension and breath flow.
benefits: Gentle extension that connects breath with posterior chain flow.
modifications: Keep the head down and use a smaller leg and arm reach.
Avoid overarching the lower back by keeping the core engaged.
progressions: Deepen the arch and lengthen the glide between movements.
Strengthen the leg press and keep the shoulder line stable.

name: Push Up
shortDescription: Dynamic core and upper-body exercise performed from a plank position with precise shoulder stacking.
focus: Shoulder stability, core endurance, and upper-body control.
benefits: Strengthens the arms, shoulders, and abdominals while reinforcing a long spine.
modifications: Keep the knees on the mat and perform the movement from a modified plank if full arm support is too intense.
Reduce the range of motion and keep the elbows closer to the rib cage to protect the shoulders.
progressions: Move to a full mat push-up with slower lowering and lifting once shoulder stability improves.
Add a controlled leg lift or alternating arm reach for a greater core challenge.

name: Footwork
shortDescription: Reformer leg pressing sequence that builds coordinated leg strength and alignment through the carriage.
benefits: Improves lower-body coordination, knee tracking, and pelvic stability.
modifications: Use lighter springs or a smaller range of motion to reduce knee strain.
Keep the heels down and focus on smooth pelvic stability throughout the press.
progressions: Increase spring tension gradually as alignment and control improve.
Explore single-leg variations on the carriage after the basic series feels stable.

name: Elephant
shortDescription: Reformer forward fold with hip hinge that mobilizes the hamstrings and challenges core control.
benefits: Enhances spinal length and shoulder stability while strengthening the posterior chain.
modifications: Shorten the stride and keep the knees soft to reduce hamstring tension.
Keep the shoulders relaxed and avoid pressing the hips too high.
progressions: Lengthen the spine and lower the heels closer to the carriage.
Increase the stretch while maintaining a strong abdominal support.

name: Mermaid
shortDescription: Side-body stretch on the chair that opens the ribcage and improves lateral mobility.
benefits: Increases flexibility in the waistline and creates more freedom in the upper body.
modifications: Keep the pelvis stable and work with a smaller reach if the ribcage or low back is sensitive.
Use the hand on the chair for support to avoid collapsing into the side body.
progressions: Lift the top arm higher and deepen the side bend once the base is stable.
Add a gentle twist toward the ceiling while keeping the spine long.

name: Push Up on Chair
shortDescription: Chair exercise that builds upper-body strength and balance with controlled shoulder loading.
benefits: Improves upper body strength and proprioception in a compact chair setting.
modifications: Use a lower spring tension or keep the hands on a stable surface if the chair feels unstable.
Limit range of motion and keep the elbows soft to protect the shoulders.
progressions: Increase the load gradually by pressing more fully through the arms with a steady torso.
Add a small leg lift or abdominal reach once shoulder control is secure.

name: Teaser on Chair
shortDescription: Chair-based teaser variation that challenges core control and balance with a seated lift.
benefits: Strengthens the abdominals while reinforcing pelvic stability and coordination.
modifications: Keep the knees bent and lift only as far as comfortable.
Use the hands on the chair for extra balance while building core support.
progressions: Extend the legs further and lengthen the spine as abdominal control improves.
Work toward a full teaser shape with a slow, supported lowering phase.

name: Push Through
shortDescription: Cadillac exercise that presses the body over the bar, strengthening the back and postural stability.
benefits: Builds spinal articulation and controlled upper-body power.
modifications: Use lighter springs and a smaller hinge range on the Cadillac.
Keep the movement slow and controlled through the spine.
progressions: Deepen the hinge and extend the shoulder line more fully.
Add a longer hold in the upper position with a steady breath.

name: Magic Circle Press
shortDescription: Mat-based prop exercise that challenges inner thigh and upper body engagement using the circle.
focus: Inner thigh strength and upper body compression.
benefits: Improves muscle tone and precision through added resistance.
modifications: Hold the circle lower and squeeze gently with less resistance.
Use a smaller range of motion for the arms to keep the shoulders soft.
progressions: Lift the circle higher and lengthen the press with stronger control.
Slow the pulse and hold the squeeze for a longer count.

name: Short Spine Massage
shortDescription: Reformer spinal articulation with leg circles that decompresses the spine and stretches the hamstrings.
benefits: Encourages deep spinal flexion and improves overall carriage control.
modifications: Keep the legs lower and move slowly through the circle while maintaining breath.
Stop before full inversion if the shoulders or low back feel compromised.
progressions: Use a slightly larger leg circle once spinal control is strong.
Add small pulsing movements for deeper pelvic articulation.

name: Knee Stretch Series
shortDescription: Reformer series performed in kneeling position that improves pelvic stability and leg alignment.
focus: Pelvic stability and posterior chain control.
benefits: Strengthens the core, glutes, and leg stabilizers in a controlled kneeling posture.
modifications: Use a softer spring setting to reduce hip and knee pressure.
Keep the hips square and limit the range of motion if the knees feel irritated.
progressions: Increase the carriage range gradually while keeping the trunk stable.
Move into the back extension variation on the same springs for added challenge.

name: Long Box Series
shortDescription: Reformer flow on the long box that targets upper body strength and back extension with carriage coordination.
focus: Upper body strength and spinal support.
benefits: Builds back extensors, shoulder stability, and proprioception on the carriage.
modifications: Use lighter springs and keep the head in line with the spine during reach.
Perform smaller range of motion on the arm exercises if the shoulders are sensitive.
progressions: Add longer arms or leg lifts once the back support is comfortable.
Increase the spring tension slightly to develop more strength through the carriage.

name: Coordination
shortDescription: A flowing Reformer sequence that combines footwork, arm coordination, and breathing for smooth carriage control.
focus: Timing, core support, and breath coordination.
benefits: Improves fluidity on the carriage while reinforcing stable alignment and respiration.
modifications: Use a lighter spring and smaller arm movements if rhythm is difficult.
Pause between each leg and arm transition to maintain a stable torso.
progressions: Gradually deepen each leg extension and arm movement while keeping the carriage smooth.
Add a slower inhalation/exhalation rhythm to accentuate control.

name: Tendon Stretch
shortDescription: Reformer exercise balancing an inverted foot position with shoulder stability and leg strength.
focus: Leg tendon stretch and shoulder support.
benefits: Builds balance, hamstring length, and coordinated upper body control.
modifications: Keep the legs lower and the hips stable if the hamstrings feel tight.
Use lighter springs and a smaller ankle range to keep the shoulders supported.
progressions: Work toward a fuller ankle stretch with a steady spine and controlled shoulder position.
Lengthen the hold once balance and comfort improve.

name: Long Spine Massage
shortDescription: Reformer spinal articulation flow that lifts the hips and elongates the spine while the feet move in a circular path.
benefits: Enhances back flexibility and promotes smooth articulation of the pelvis and spine.
modifications: Keep the legs lower and less inverted if the hamstrings or back feel sensitive.
Move slowly through the circle and maintain steady breathing.
progressions: Increase the circle height once spinal control is secure.
Add a gentle hip lift articulation with each breath for deeper mobilization.

name: Stomach Massage (Round Back)
shortDescription: Classic Reformer series that strengthens the core and improves carriage control with a rounded spine.
focus: Core stability and articulated spine control.
benefits: Develops abdominal support, breath coordination, and smooth leg carriage movement.
modifications: Use lighter springs and keep a short range of motion if the abdominals feel sensitive.
Slow the leg movements and focus on ribcage stabilization through the entire sequence.
progressions: Increase the range of movement and work toward a longer carriage cycle with controlled breath.
Hold the legs slightly higher or use a lower tension spring for a deeper challenge.

name: Stomach Massage (Flat Back)
shortDescription: Reformer variation emphasizing a flat back for abdominal strength and pelvic stability.
focus: Core endurance and neutral spine support.
benefits: Builds strength in the deep abdominals while promoting a stable, supported torso.
modifications: Shorten the range of motion and keep the head relaxed to avoid neck strain.
Use a softer spring setting and pause at each leg change to reinforce stability.
progressions: Increase the carriage range and coordinate with breathing for smoother transitions.
Try longer leg extensions once the lower abs feel secure and supported.

name: Roll Down Bar
shortDescription: Cadillac exercise that focuses on spinal articulation while moving the torso over the bar in a controlled roll-down.
benefits: Improves deep core control and encourages smooth spinal mobility.
modifications: Start with a smaller range and keep the shoulders relaxed away from the ears.
Use a softer spring or lighter resistance if the upper back feels tight.
progressions: Increase the roll-down depth with a slower cadence.
Add arm reach variations while maintaining spinal length and control.

name: Arm Springs
shortDescription: Cadillac upper-body sequence using springs to build shoulder mobility and control.
benefits: Improves controlled arm movement and upper-body coordination through spring resistance.
modifications: Use lighter springs and keep the elbows slightly bent to reduce strain.
Work with smaller arm arcs until the shoulders feel stable.
progressions: Increase the range of motion and add slower transitions for more shoulder control.
Experiment with higher spring tension once the movement feels secure.

name: Leg Springs
shortDescription: Cadillac leg spring series that strengthens the legs while maintaining pelvic stability.
benefits: Builds coordinated lower-body control with spring resistance and stable pelvis alignment.
modifications: Use lighter spring tension and keep the movement slow if the hips feel sensitive.
Keep the legs in a smaller range of motion and keep the spine supported.
progressions: Increase the spring tension gradually as control improves.
Try longer leg circles or lifts with a steady pelvis.

name: Pilates Ring Squeeze
shortDescription: Prop-based inner thigh and upper body exercise using the circle to create controlled resistance.
focus: Inner thigh strength and upper body stability.
benefits: Adds accessible resistance for improved muscle engagement and precision.
modifications: Use a lighter squeeze and focus on keeping the pelvis stable.
Hold the ring lightly if wrist or shoulder tension is present.
progressions: Increase the squeeze resistance as control improves.
Combine the ring squeeze with longer arm movements for an added challenge.

name: Ball Roll
shortDescription: Supine ball exercise that massages the spine and challenges balance while strengthening the core.
benefits: Enhances proprioception, coordination, and controlled movement with a small Pilates ball.
modifications: Use a smaller ball and keep the legs closer to the body for greater support.
Move more slowly through each roll to maintain stability.
progressions: Roll with longer legs or a larger ball once control improves.
Add a small pause at the top of each roll to engage the deep core.

name: Resistance Band Arm Series
shortDescription: Standing or seated band sequence that strengthens the arms and shoulders with portable resistance.
focus: Upper body strength and scapular stability.
benefits: Improves shoulder control and arm endurance using easy-to-use prop resistance.
modifications: Use lighter band tension and keep the movements small if the shoulders are sensitive.
Perform the series seated for extra stability.
progressions: Increase band tension or add longer reaches as control improves.
Combine the band series with core bracing for a full-body challenge.

name: Single Straight Leg Stretch
shortDescription: Alternating straight-leg scissors motion performed supine that builds core stability and hip flexor control.
focus: Lower abdominal strength and hip flexor engagement.
benefits: Develops core control while stretching the hamstrings and hip flexors alternately.
modifications: Keep the head on the mat and reduce the leg range if the lower back arches.
Slow the alternation to focus on spinal stability before adding speed.
progressions: Lower both legs closer to the mat while keeping the pelvis stable.
Increase the speed of the alternation while maintaining a steady breath.

name: Double Straight Leg Stretch
shortDescription: Supine double-leg lowering and lifting that challenges deep abdominal strength under a long-lever load.
focus: Lower abdominal and deep core strength.
benefits: Builds lower abdominal endurance and lumbo-pelvic stability under load.
modifications: Keep the hands behind the head for neck support and raise the legs higher.
Bend the knees to reduce the lever arm if the lower back lifts from the mat.
progressions: Lower the legs progressively closer to the mat while keeping the spine imprinted.
Add a small lower-leg pulse at the bottom of the range before lifting.

name: Criss Cross
shortDescription: Supine rotational exercise alternating oblique reach toward opposite knee for waist definition and core control.
benefits: Targets the obliques and encourages thoracic rotation while stabilizing the pelvis.
modifications: Keep the twisting range small and avoid pulling the neck with the hands.
Move slowly and pause at the top of each rotation to control the motion.
progressions: Extend the bottom leg lower while maintaining the rotation to increase core demand.
Add a small pulse at the peak of each rotation before switching sides.

name: Plank
shortDescription: Static full-body hold in a straight line from head to heels that trains overall core endurance and alignment.
benefits: Builds isometric core and shoulder stability while reinforcing a neutral spine.
modifications: Drop to the knees to reduce the load on the core and shoulders.
Raise the hands onto a block or chair to lower intensity.
progressions: Add a single-arm or single-leg lift while maintaining a stable plank.
Increase the hold duration or transition directly into a Leg Pull Front.

name: Rowing Series
shortDescription: A family of six seated arm-spring exercises on the Reformer that develop back strength, posture, and shoulder mobility through pulling and pressing patterns.
focus: Back strength, shoulder mobility, and upright posture.
benefits: Strengthens the back extensors and posterior shoulder girdle while opening the chest.
modifications: Use lighter spring resistance and reduce the range of arm motion initially.
Keep the spine tall against a wall or footbar for positional feedback.
progressions: Add a forward hinge and reach at the end of each pulling pattern.
Increase spring resistance as back strength and shoulder mobility improve.

name: Short Box Series
shortDescription: A seated box sequence on the Reformer integrating spinal flexion, extension, rotation, and lateral flexion for complete spinal mobility.
focus: Spinal mobility in all planes and core control.
benefits: Trains the spine in flexion, extension, rotation, and lateral flexion while seated on an unstable surface.
modifications: Reduce the range in each direction and keep hands lightly touching the box for support.
Perform the round-back and flat-back variations before adding rotation.
progressions: Add a full side bend or twist with arm reach to deepen the range.
Perform the tree variation to combine hip flexor stretch with spinal articulation.

name: Running
shortDescription: Alternating heel raise and lower on the Reformer that mimics a running stride to mobilize the ankles and cool down the legs.
benefits: Mobilizes the ankles, stretches the calves, and gently reintegrates the legs after carriage work.
modifications: Slow the alternation and focus on controlled heel lowering to ease calf tightness.
Keep the motion small if the Achilles tendons feel tight.
progressions: Increase the speed to a light jogging rhythm while maintaining pelvis stability.
Add a small hip hinge to intensify the calf stretch at the end of each stride.

name: Semi-Circle
shortDescription: A flowing arc movement on the Reformer that combines hip extension, spinal articulation, and shoulder stability in one continuous loop.
focus: Hip extension, spinal articulation, and shoulder stability.
benefits: Promotes smooth lumbo-pelvic mobility and hip flexor release through a dynamic arc.
modifications: Reduce the range of the arc and keep the hips higher than the knees throughout.
Move slowly through each phase and avoid dropping the hips below alignment.
progressions: Slow the pace to challenge control through the hanging position.
Focus on precise spinal articulation bone by bone on the descent.

name: Backstroke
shortDescription: Supine arm-and-leg coordination exercise on the Reformer that mirrors a swimming backstroke pattern to open the chest and challenge core control.
focus: Chest opening, shoulder mobility, and full-body coordination.
benefits: Opens the anterior chain, improves shoulder mobility, and develops coordination of simultaneous limb movement.
modifications: Perform the arms or legs separately before combining the movement.
Keep the head on the headrest to reduce cervical strain.
progressions: Add a pause at full extension before returning to the starting position.
Slow the return phase to maximise control and spring resistance.

name: Pulling Straps
shortDescription: Prone back extension exercise on the Reformer long box in which the arms pull the straps to lift the chest and strengthen the back.
focus: Back extension strength and posterior shoulder engagement.
benefits: Strengthens the thoracic extensors and posterior deltoids while opening the chest.
modifications: Keep the lift small and focus on length rather than height.
Use a lighter spring and avoid compressing the lower back at the top.
progressions: Increase the lift height and hold briefly at the top.
Combine with a T position (arms wide) for added posterior shoulder work.

name: Down Stretch
shortDescription: Kneeling plank-to-pike transition on the Reformer that mobilizes the spine and builds shoulder and core stability.
benefits: Builds shoulder girdle stability and a long, controlled spinal extension under load.
modifications: Keep the knees on a pad and limit the range of carriage travel.
Focus on a long spine rather than maximum range.
progressions: Increase the carriage travel distance as shoulder stability improves.
Transition directly into Up Stretch for a flowing sequence.

name: Up Stretch
shortDescription: Pike-to-plank transition on the Reformer that stretches the posterior chain and challenges balanced shoulder and core control.
benefits: Stretches the hamstrings and calves while building shoulder stability in a dynamic pike.
modifications: Bend the knees slightly to reduce hamstring load.
Limit the carriage travel to maintain a long spine.
progressions: Deepen the pike and push the heels back further.
Slow the transition from pike to plank to increase eccentric shoulder control.

name: Snake
shortDescription: Rotational side-plank and spine-extension exercise on the Reformer that challenges advanced core stability and full-body coordination.
focus: Lateral core stability and rotational strength.
benefits: Develops advanced rotational strength along the entire kinetic chain.
modifications: Keep the range small and focus on maintaining a square shoulder position.
Practice the entry and exit positions separately before adding the full movement.
progressions: Increase the carriage travel and hold the side plank briefly at the end range.
Combine Snake and Twist in a flowing sequence for added challenge.

name: Front Splits
shortDescription: Standing lunge stretch on the Reformer that deeply opens the hip flexors and challenges balance while reinforcing core engagement.
focus: Hip flexor length and standing balance.
benefits: Provides a deep hip flexor and quad stretch while building single-leg balance and stability.
modifications: Keep the front foot on the platform and limit the lunge depth.
Hold onto the footbar for balance support initially.
progressions: Increase the lunge depth and allow the carriage to travel further.
Release the footbar and balance freely in the lunge position.

name: Side Splits
shortDescription: Standing lateral stretch on the Reformer that opens the inner thighs and challenges hip abductor strength and balance.
focus: Inner thigh length and hip abductor strength.
benefits: Stretches the adductors and builds lateral hip stability in a weight-bearing position.
modifications: Keep the range of movement small and stand close to the footbar for stability.
Use the footbar as a light support until balance improves.
progressions: Increase the split range and slow the return to challenge adductor eccentric strength.
Add a small torso rotation or arm reach to increase the balance challenge.

name: Overhead
shortDescription: Supine inversion exercise on the Reformer that lifts the legs overhead while the core controls the carriage, building deep abdominal and back strength.
focus: Deep core strength and spinal articulation under inversion.
benefits: Challenges extreme core control and spinal articulation through a full overhead position.
modifications: Keep the legs at 90 degrees and only lift the hips slightly.
Avoid if there is any neck or cervical spine sensitivity.
progressions: Work toward a fully vertical leg position while controlling the carriage.
Slow the lowering phase to increase eccentric core demand.

name: Balance Point
shortDescription: Advanced seated balance challenge on the Reformer that stabilizes in a V-sit on the moving carriage while engaged with the straps.
focus: Balance, core stability, and hip flexor control.
benefits: Develops exceptional balance and core engagement on an unstable, moving surface.
modifications: Keep the feet lightly touching the footbar for stability.
Reduce the arm and leg movements until core balance is established.
progressions: Remove foot contact and balance freely on the carriage.
Add arm circles or leg variations to increase the destabilization challenge.

name: Tower
shortDescription: Supine vertical leg press against a spring bar on the Cadillac that builds core and hip strength through a full overhead extension.
focus: Core strength and hip flexor coordination.
benefits: Develops core stability and hip control under resistance through an overhead position.
modifications: Keep the legs slightly bent and avoid pressing past the bar.
Reduce spring tension to allow a comfortable range of motion.
progressions: Press the legs to a fully vertical position and slow the return.
Add a spinal roll-down at the end for combined articulation.

name: Cat Stretch on Cadillac
shortDescription: Kneeling spinal flexion and extension on the Cadillac using the push-through bar to guide deep spinal mobilization.
benefits: Mobilizes the full length of the spine in both flexion and extension with spring-assisted guidance.
modifications: Keep the range small and focus on one spinal segment at a time.
Use a lighter spring to reduce the resistance on the bar.
progressions: Increase the arc of both flexion and extension.
Slow the transition between cat and cow to deepen segmental control.

name: Hanging
shortDescription: Standing traction exercise on the Cadillac using the roll-down bar or trapeze for spinal decompression and shoulder mobility.
focus: Spinal decompression and shoulder girdle mobility.
benefits: Decompresses the spine and mobilizes the shoulder girdle through supported hanging.
modifications: Keep the feet touching the floor for partial weight support.
Limit the hang duration and avoid if shoulder instability is present.
progressions: Lift the feet from the floor and hold a free hang.
Add gentle knee lifts or hip circles to increase the traction effect.

name: Going Up Front
shortDescription: Single-leg press on the Wunda Chair facing the chair that builds unilateral leg strength, balance, and core control.
benefits: Develops unilateral lower-body strength and balance in a functional standing position.
modifications: Hold onto the chair handles for support while learning the movement.
Reduce the pedal depth to limit the range of motion.
progressions: Release the hands and maintain balance without support.
Add a slow, controlled press and lower to increase eccentric demand.

name: Going Up Side
shortDescription: Lateral single-leg press on the Wunda Chair that targets hip abductors, adductors, and lateral core stability.
focus: Lateral hip stability and single-leg strength.
benefits: Builds lateral hip strength and challenges frontal-plane balance and core stability.
modifications: Hold the chair frame and limit the range of the pedal press.
Keep the supporting foot flat to increase the base of support.
progressions: Release the hand support to increase the balance challenge.
Slow the return phase to increase lateral hip eccentric work.

name: Pumping
shortDescription: Seated or standing rhythmic pedal press on the Wunda Chair that challenges core endurance and limb coordination through repeated spring resistance.
focus: Core endurance and limb coordination under spring load.
benefits: Builds rhythmic coordination and core endurance through repetitive resistance work.
modifications: Use a light spring and focus on maintaining an upright spine.
Perform seated before progressing to standing variations.
progressions: Increase the spring resistance as coordination and strength improve.
Combine with arm movements to add an upper-body coordination challenge.

name: Achilles Stretch
shortDescription: Standing heel drop off the Wunda Chair pedal that stretches the calf complex and Achilles tendon under controlled spring tension.
benefits: Lengthens the gastrocnemius and soleus while building ankle stability under load.
modifications: Keep the stretch gentle and avoid forcing the heel below the pedal.
Hold the chair frame for balance support.
progressions: Deepen the heel drop and hold at the end range for longer.
Perform single-leg to increase the stretch intensity.

name: Foam Roller Series
shortDescription: A sequence of spinal, hip, and shoulder mobility exercises performed on a foam roller to improve balance, body awareness, and fascial release.
focus: Spinal mobility, balance, and soft tissue release.
benefits: Improves proprioception, releases myofascial tension, and supports spinal alignment.
modifications: Perform exercises next to a wall for balance support.
Start with supine exercises before progressing to seated or standing variations.
progressions: Remove wall support and perform exercises in free balance.
Add arm or leg movements to increase the stability challenge.

name: Arc Barrel Series
shortDescription: A collection of spinal extension, flexion, and side-bend exercises performed over the arc barrel to increase range of motion and back strength.
focus: Spinal extension and lateral flexion range of motion.
benefits: Opens the thoracic spine, strengthens the back extensors, and improves lateral flexibility.
modifications: Reduce the arc amplitude by placing a folded mat under the barrel.
Support the lower back and limit the extension range.
progressions: Increase the range of extension and side bend as mobility improves.
Add arm reaches and rotation to deepen the spinal work.

name: Spine Corrector Series
shortDescription: A suite of exercises on the spine corrector barrel that combines spinal articulation, hip opening, and shoulder mobilization for postural rebalancing.
benefits: Corrects postural imbalances, opens the chest, and develops segmental spinal control.
modifications: Keep the range of motion small and avoid compressing the lower back.
Use a cushion under the tailbone for additional support.
progressions: Add arm circles or leg variations to the foundational exercises.
Combine extension and rotation for more advanced spinal patterning.
